title: Choose the visual world for the frogbot dashboard
question: The roll assigned the Git Graph Rail. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Git Graph Rail
options.lineage: git log --graph, the commit rail every engineer reads daily
options.thesis: Runs are commits on a rail. The rail's continuity is the health of the system: an unbroken line means reviews are flowing, a cut at HEAD means the credential died. Refuses the card-grid dashboard with stat tiles.
options.viewport: A single content column. Top strip: owner/repo as a mono ref, then Runs · Settings · Credentials as plain tabs. Below, the rail runs down the left edge of the column with one node per run; the newest at top under a HEAD marker that doubles as the health banner. Each row: PR number as a ref pill, title, kind, who triggered it, elapsed, tokens; the node glyph is the state (filled dot done, rotating ring in progress, crossed dot failed, hollow queued, slashed cancelled). An incremental review draws a lane back to the review it extends. Primary action lives in the row: open the PR, open the Actions log.
options.risk: Reads like a git client if the rail turns decorative. The lane connecting incremental reviews must be real data or the metaphor is a costume.

raised.raise: Colour confined to the hairline: only the rail and state glyphs carry hue; every text field stays achromatic.
The accent is reserved for the active leg: only the in-progress run wears the rail colour; finished runs are ink.
Sections separated by real gaps, never by card borders: the page is one sheet with deep quiet between blocks.
Palette law: exactly five state glyphs, no intermediate hues, no tinted backgrounds for status.

options.label: Departures Board
options.thesis: Every run is a departure: time, PR, destination, status in a fixed-width row, and a state change flips the flap. The clearest 'did my thing run' surface there is.
options.viewport: A dark board filling the width: columns TIME · PR · KIND · STATUS, rows in strict pitch, the status column flipping on change. Settings and credentials are boards of their own below a thin header.
options.risk: The most familiar status metaphor; many runs in this category land here, and the flip animation is decoration the moment it stops carrying a real state change.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The layout grid stays visible; every row, glyph and control snaps to its cells. Engineers read graph paper natively.
options.viewport: Faint grid hairlines across the sheet; the runs list is a table whose rows are exact cell multiples; the repo name set large from grid cells.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: rows and settings snap to cells and the grid is honest structure. Holds product clarity; loses on identification, since the audience reads git graphs, not type specimens.
options.risk: Becomes wallpaper if the grid is not load-bearing.

options.label: Cutting Bench Select Rail
options.lineage: film cutting bench and select rail
options.thesis: A perforated rail crossing the sheet; each run a punched frame; state is a mark, not a hue.
options.viewport: A horizontal rail of frames at fixed pitch, the frame you left flagged, discarded runs hung on pins below.
options.case: Holds product clarity: 'state is a mark' is exactly the product principle. Loses identification; nobody on the team has cut film, and the orange-on-black field fights daylight phone use.
options.risk: Reads as a theme on a phone in daylight.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: diffraction fringe on a forming cloud
options.case: Loses both axes: the audience does not identify with atmospheric optics and pastel bands blur status.
options.kept: Colour confined to hairline edges while the text field stays achromatic.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.case: Loses both: terrain inks carry no product meaning here and the legend is a second vocabulary to learn.
options.kept: One colour reserved for the active leg only.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.case: Loses both: a surreal construction world for a status tool obscures the task.
options.kept: Sections stacked as blocks with deep gaps, never boxed.

options.label: CRT Arcade Pixel Glow
options.case: Loses both: novelty grammar and glow fight legibility on a phone in daylight.
options.kept: Strict palette law: a fixed set of state colours and nothing in between.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A SaaS admin: left sidebar, white content cards, blue primary button, a row of stat tiles above a table. Executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar with three items; a header with the repo name; four stat tiles; the runs table beneath.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other internal tool by design.
